docs.summary:
The project-wide navigation area table: up to 32 named areas with per-area path costs, addressed by index and combined into 32-bit masks. Area 0 is Walkable, 1 is Not Walkable, 2 is Jump; 3..31 are user-defined.

Detour stores area `i` as `i + 1`, because its 0 is the null area meaning "not part of the navmesh". [`ToDetourArea`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAreas~ToDetourArea) / [`FromDetourArea`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAreas~FromDetourArea) are the only places that offset is applied — never hand-roll it. Bake-side conversions go through `ProwlInputGeomProvider.DetourAreaFor`, which additionally maps [`NotWalkable`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAreas~NotWalkable) to the null area; calling [`ToDetourArea`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAreas~ToDetourArea) on a source area instead silently resurrects traversable "Not Walkable" polys.
Maximum number of areas (indices 0..31), the width of an area mask.
The built-in default walkable area index.
The built-in not-walkable area index. Geometry marked with this area is excluded from the navmesh entirely.
The built-in area index used for jump/off-mesh connections.
The cost an area starts with before any project settings apply. The navigation settings page seeds a new project from this too, so the two cannot disagree.
Get the name of an area, or an empty string for unnamed user areas.

docs.summary: Set the default path cost multiplier for an area. Clamped to >= 1: Detour's A* heuristic (straight-line distance) is only admissible when no traversal is cheaper than distance itself, so costs below 1 would silently produce suboptimal paths. To express "agents prefer this area", raise every OTHER area's cost above 1 instead.
